articleTitle: LoRa-Based Asset Tracking System with Data Encryption Using AES-256 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In general, organizations have a set of secured physical assets- However, the possibility of theft is still there, so an Asset Tracking System is needed to help asset owners detect and track the position of stolen assets. We made an asset tracking system which consists of a transmitter (placed on the asset) and a receiver (placed in the monitoring room). The communication between the transmitter and the receiver is based on LoRa with a frequency of 920-923 MHz by implementing the AES-256 cryptographic algorithm to guarantee its safety from any possible eavesdropper or attacks, which can ultimately threaten the confidentiality of the communication. The system we built can detect theft and track assets with 100% accuracy from a distance of 28.38 meters until the communication is lost, i.e., more than 10.22 kilometers in LOS conditions, 400 meters in NLOS with tree obstructions, and 350 meters in NLOS conditions with building obstacles. We have also demonstrated that the communications are secure from Eavesdropper attacks.

articleTitle: A Novel Rule for Designing Tri-Stages Piecewise Linear NLFM Chirp
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Chirp waveform is essential to a radar system with pulse compression technique. Various Nonlinear Frequency Modulation (NLFM) chirp waveforms have been proposed to suppress sidelobes that are relatively high in the Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) chirp waveform. One type of them is the Piecewise Linear NLFM (PWL-NLFM) that can be viewed as a concatenation of several LFM stages with a different chirp rate. The challenge in using this is figuring out the chirp rate for each stage. In this paper, a rule for determining the chirp rate for each stage value of the Tri-Stages PWL-NLFM (TS-PWL-NLFM), a particular type of PWL-NLFM, is proposed. Snippet code in GNU Octave for generating the discrete-time TS-PWL-NLFM waveform as well as for calculating the matched filtering in order to evaluate the designed chips are presented. Besides, numerical examples run show its superiority sidelobes reduction compared to the LFM and the existing results.

articleTitle: Estimating MQTT Performance in A Virtual Testbed of INA-CBT Communication Sub-System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Indonesia Cable Based Tsunameter (INA-CBT) is a network of seafloor sensors interconnected by fiber optic cables that is used as a tsunami detection system. All sensor data are aggregated at landing stations and then sent to a central or read down station for further processing. Currently, Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) is utilized for the application-layer communication protocol between landing stations and a read down station. Due to limited network infrastructures in some regional areas in Indonesia, it is necessary to know the required network parameters before deploying this system with certain quality targets. This paper presents some experimental results in a virtual testbed modeling a simplified INA-CBT system, and provides some insights on the achievable latency with its required minimal bottleneck bandwidth and MQTT Quality of Service (QoS) level.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, and Characterization of PVA-SnO2 based Humidity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this research, humidity sensors based on Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA)-Tin Oxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) have been designed and fabricated using thick film technology. Fabrication of the sensor devices was conducted using screen printing techniques on Alumina (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) substrates with Silver (Ag) as the electrode material. The number of fingers on the electrodes was varied from 4 to 8 to obtain different resistance values of the sensor. SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> was added to the PVA sensing layer with variations in the composition of 1:1 and 1:2. The fabricated sensor devices have been tested under various humidity points and temperatures inside a custom chamber having a reference humidity sensor. The results showed that all sensors responded well to humidity variation by decreasing in resistance values as the relative humidity (RH) points were increased from 50 to 90%. However, temperature variation from 25 to 35 °C has resulted in higher responses for all sensors at each RH point. Although the sensors with composition of the sensitive layers of 1:2 had shown more sensitive responses compared to those with 1:1 composition, overall sensors have demonstrated fast responses to humidity variations with response time of less than 3 min (167 s) and recovery time of less than 10 min (559 s).

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Diagnosis of Time-Modulated Arrays Based on Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is proposed for diagnosing impaired time-modulated arrays (TMAs). The TMA diagnosis problem is modeled as a sparse recovery problem for the equivalent excitations at the center frequency and each harmonic frequency based on compressive sensing (CS). Then, a mixed l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-norm minimization method is proposed to realize the multi-frequency joint diagnosis. The proposed method can improve the diagnosis accuracy and reduce the number of spatial samples compared with the isolated single frequency diagnosis methods. Numerical examples and successful comparisons indicate that the proposed method has a good prospect in the application of TMAs.

articleTitle: An Improved Rainfall Detection of Rain Radar Using High-Precision Circuit and Speckle Filtering
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Two rain scanner radars modified from a marine radar have been operated to observe precipitation over Bandung city. The recorded observation data revealed instability in the clutter removal products. One of the main factors contributing to the instability is the precision of the pulse signal conversion results before analog-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling. This factor contributes to the increase of speckle numbers in the radar image. In this research, a high-precision circuit and speckle filtering algorithm are proposed to improve rainfall detection. The proposed high-speed and precision circuit consist of a voltage divider and a unity gain circuit utilizing a high-speed and low-noise operational amplifier. The measurement results reveal that the rise and fall times performed by the operational amplifier show a significant improvement closer to the input signal (original radar signal). It also does not produce an overshoot and presents a high percentage of settling time (steeper). The results of rain detection using radar with a high-precision circuit has higher reflectivity values until 40 dBZ. It has a higher sensitivity, indicated by the more significant amount of detected rain with higher intensity. The device also contributes to minimizing the speckle occurrence, thus easing the work of the speckle filtering. The filtering has been tested and successfully removed the speckles below 5 × 5 pixel width.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Injection Control of Isolated DC-DC Converter for Cable-based Seabed Observatory Platform
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The paper presents the control of current-fed isolated step-down direct current to direct current (DC-DC) converter that will be used as power supply unit in cable-based seabed observatory platform, which is placed several kilometers from shore. Steady-state and dynamic model of converter are developed, which here is different to step-down buck converter. The injection proposed can linearize the system even that the load is unknown. The stability is proven by Lyapunov function and the controllability is analyzed. The simulation using Simscape -Simulink shows the stability and convergence of output voltage around 24V DC desired with 300mA current source, and output current up to 5A even for several converters in shunt.

articleTitle: Identification of Potential Electromagnetic Disturbances at 2172 MHz in Autonomous EV Routes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The increased use of Autonomous Electric Vehicles (AEV) and wireless mobile and broadcast communication results in the potential electromagnetic (EM) disturbance of the off-board EM source into the electronics component of AEV. This potential EM disturbance may disturb the communication, navigation and surveillance functions in the AEV electronic modules. Therefore, it is necessary to plan a route that minimizes the potential EM disturbance by choosing a path with less disturbance of the EM field. This paper provides potential EM disturbance measurement results at 2172 MHz along a chosen path on the campus of a Research Centre in a suburb area of Jakarta. The chosen frequency is one of the frequency ranges mentioned in CISPR 25. The measurements were performed using a broadband field meter which gives the EM field strength along the chosen route. The results show that the measured potential EM disturbance values vary due to the surrounding vegetation, building and EM infrastructures.

articleTitle: Characteristic of Circular Patch Antennas Using Open and Close Metal Rings on Artificial Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study explores the characteristics of circular patch antennas. If the patch antenna generally uses natural dielectric material, the proposed circular patch antenna uses artificial dielectric material. The dielectric properties of natural materials have been modified by adding metallic layers in open and closed rings of one and two layers. This study is based on simulation results using the CST Suites Studio. Simulations were carried out at a frequency of 3.3 - 3.7 GHz on the Lucite substrate. The substrate has a relative permittivity of 3.4 and a thickness of 1.5 mm. Based on the simulation, it is obtained that a circular patch antenna with two strips of open ring metal has the widest bandwidth of 196 MHz for a return loss greater than 10 dB and the highest gain of 6.4 dBi. In addition, open ring metal has the potential to miniaturize the circular patch antenna size by up to 32.08%.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Inkjet-Printed Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) Polystyrene Sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) Sensing Film on Flexible Substrate for Humidity Sensor Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)

authors.preferredName: Syed Muhammad Hafiz Syed Mohd Jaafar

abstract: This work presents a preliminary study towards the fabrication and characterisation of a printed humidity sensor to be integrated into a chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) device. The sensing element of the humidity sensor has been developed using poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate PEDOT:PSS as the sensing film and graphene-based inks as the conductive track on flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate through inkjet printing technique. From this study, it has been shown that the sensor is capable of detecting humidity changes ranging from 18% to 85% with a 2-layer printing of PEDOT:PSS sensing film.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Frequency Reconfigurable Anechoic Chamber Based on Omnidirectional Reflectionless Absorption Spatial Kramers-Kronig Medium
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Ideal microwave absorbers capable of broadband omnidirectional reflectionless absorption have been an important subject of scientific research for centuries. Recently, theoretical studies have shown that spatial Kramers-Kronig (KK) media can achieve omnidirectional reflectionless absorption without the use of any gain element. In this paper, the concept of spatial KK relation to cylindrical coordinates is extending and a dual-Lorentz-resonance space-frequency KK permittivity profile is implemented in order to achieve impedance matching to free space. To further extend the absorption spectrum, tunable varactors are introduced into the unit cell to change Lorentz-resonance frequency, and thus, the operating frequency can be reconfigured in a wide frequency range. A two-dimensional (2D) 48-cm-diameter doughnut-shaped anechoic chamber is implemented using the designed cylindrical frequency reconfigurable spatial KK medium. The simulated result shows that a reconfigurable frequency range from 4.5 GHz to 5.25 GHz is realized. Our method paves a new way to design ideal microwave absorber, especially demanding wide-angle incidence and broad bandwidth.

articleTitle: Simulating Labuan Bajo Indonesia Cable Based Tsunameter (INA-CBT) Landing Station Network through the Development of IPFIX-based Traffic Generator Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In a complex modern technology, a single application may include multiple technologies with various transport mechanisms. Delivering approaches to simulate these mechanisms, traffic generators are introduced to mimic real congestion in a measurable environment. Ensuring system reliability, the third-generation INA-CBT (Indonesia Cable-Based Tsunameter) infrastructure is equipped with an IPFIX-based monitoring system that was installed in the Landing Station (LS) and Read Down Station (RDS) areas. Hence, in this paper, we introduce our preliminary work on developing IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) protocol-based traffic generator tools. Combined with our INA-CBT system testbed, this application development aims at providing a deep-through analysis of traffic behavior in the INA-CBT’s LS. We developed three python-based subsystem modules, i.e., the data reader, data parser, and data receiver modules. In conclusion, from the test results, the error rate percentage reproduced by the traffic generator tools compared with the real LS traffic reached almost 16.265% and 28.649% for Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) data, respectively. However, compared to the real traffic pattern, the application already has the ability to impersonate TCP and UDP type traffic for each flow time sequence in an acceptable error rate range (<30%).

articleTitle: Design of Circular Polarization Microstrip Patch Antenna Combined with Conical Horn
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This study presents a simulation of an S-Band communication ground station antenna system with a circularly polarized microstrip antenna and a double-arm feeding line. It considers a substrate with a relative permittivity of 2.2 and a thickness of 1.575 mm to design the proposed antenna. One of the most crucial aspects of an antenna with circular polarization is its axial ratio. This proposed antenna uses a double-arm feeding line with an aperture connected between the patch and the feeding line. The power transfer occurs by electromagnetic coupling to achieve circular polarization. At a frequency of 2.3 GHz, the gain of the conical horn and microstrip patch antenna is 9.468 dB. This return loss value ranges from 2.288 to 2.31 GHz at a threshold of -10 dB. With a 3 dB limit, the axial ratio achieved a bandwidth frequency of 2.271-2.308 GHz. It shows a good performance for further research and implementation.

articleTitle: Over 10% Efficient CuIn(S,Se)2 Thin Film Solar Cells Fabricated from Molecular Precursor Ink
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: We report the fabrication of solution-processed CuIn(S,Se)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film solar cells based on deposition from molecular ink. These thin films were produced by spin coating of ink containing CuCl, InCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, and thiourea dissolved in methanol, followed by selenization at high temperatures. X-ray diffraction analysis suggests that the as-coated film was low-crystalline CuInS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> which converted into high-crystalline mixed sulfur-selenium CuIn(S,Se)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> alloy after the selenization process at 550 °C. Solar cells were fabricated from CISSe films by coating with a CdS layer (chemical bath deposition) and ZnO/ITO bilayers (sputtering). The device showed a power conversion efficiency of 8.3% (Jsc : 35.17 mA cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>: 0.43 V, FF: 54.81%). After modification of the spin coating process, power conversion efficiency as high as 10.10% (Jsc : 36.51 mA cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>: 0.45 V, FF: 61.09%, no anti-reflection coating) was achieved from the device using a relatively thick CISSe film (~3.8 µm).

articleTitle: Anti-resonance Suppression on A Quartz Crystal Microbalance Sensor for Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The existence of shunt capacitance in Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) structure leads appearance of anti-resonance in the spectral response. The anti-resonance leads to higher impedance than the mechanical resonance, affecting the primary frequency resonant determination. In this work, a reference spectral subtraction method was applied to remove the effect of passive capacitance on the resonance spectra of a QCM sensor. Principally, a reference spectral was subtracted from the sensor spectral using a particular calculation, resulting in optimized/compensated spectral responses. Furthermore, an antibody layer could be immobilized on the employed QCM to detect protein or virus agents. A propitious resonance shifting of 6.4 kHz was obtained by immobilizing the antibody layer on the QCM sensor. Hence, it leads to an excellent potency to further develop QCM-based biosensors.

articleTitle: Development of the NOAA-19 Satellite Data Receiver Ingest System based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The issue of mastery of the ingest system is important because ingest cards are a "key component" that is not traded except in one system package. Therefore, through mastery of this component, changes in data transmission rate will be followed continuously as long as the COTS component is available. Currently, a satellite data transmission system is in progress from band L to band X, which has an impact on increasing the data transmission rate from 1 to 6 Mbps to 15 to 80 Mbps. To overcome these problems, an intermediate technology was developed by designing an ingest system based on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) supported by several modular boards and can be reconfigure to get higher capability/speed. The FPGA board functions to receive data and clock streams of the NOAA-19 satellite from the demodulator serially and forward it to the personal computer (PC) via a Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART) output unit. The output of this ingest system design is a RAW data file to be further processed into level-0 products by PC Ingest. Implementing the ingest system is expected to reduce the dependence on purchasing commercial ingest cards.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor Based on Kretschmann Configuration for Dengue Virus Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) has been extensively used as a diagnostic tool for virus and bacteria detection (biosensors). This research detected dengue virus (DENV) using a non-structural-1 monoclonal antibody (NS-1 mAb) on the gold/EDC-NHS/IgG component of SPR. The experiment was conducted in real-time by monitoring the SPR angle and response unit (RU) change. As a result, it was observed that the presence of the functional molecule on the SPR chip caused the shift of the SPR angle to the higher incident angle, indicating a refractive index change proportional to the attached molecule layer. The increase of RU value due to the injection of the biomolecule into the SPR chip represents the SPR angle shift. The result revealed the potential of the SPR as a promising tool for DENV detection.

articleTitle: Free-Standing Carbon Electrode Modified by Polyvinyl Alcohol for Efficient HTM-Free Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A free-standing polyvinyl-alcohol (PVA)-modified carbon film with good conductivity has been developed and applied in hole transport material (HTM)-free perovskite solar cells. This free-standing carbon film was hot-pressed onto the methylammonium lead iodide-based perovskite layer as the back contact electrode. Adding PVA during solvent treatment is expected to increase the flexibility and conductivity of the carbon electrodes. An HTM-free perovskite solar cell with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 2.83% was obtained, which is higher than a similar cell prepared without PVA modification. This free-standing carbon-modified PVA electrode has the advantages of a low-cost, simple preparation process and shows great feasibility for the up-scaling of perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: Design Flexible Microstrip Antenna for Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease characterized by high blood sugar (glucose) levels. This research was conducted in line with the high urgency to no longer use invasive techniques in checking blood sugar levels. Therefore, it is necessary to design a tool that can detect blood sugar levels without injuring the body by non-invasive methods. This paper creates a flexible antenna sensor using a flexible substrate of Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) with a thickness of 0.135 mm. Silver nano-ink with a thickness of 0.01 mm was used as a patch, ground, and feedline material. The feeding technique used in the design of this antenna model is a coplanar waveguide (CPW). The antenna is proposed as a sensor for blood glucose detection using saliva samples. In this paper, the antenna is modeled with a circular patch form. The simulation shows that the proposed antenna works well at 2.45 GHz with a bidirectional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Sparse Channel Estimation Using Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) for MIMO-OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The OFDM is a multicarrier technique that is well-known for its capability to cope with highly time-variant wireless channel. When combined with a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique, MIMO-OFDM system can offer reliable high data rate transmission over broadband wireless channels. In such system, the availability of channel state information (CSI) is critical issue that will determine overall performance of the system. CSI is commonly acquired through pilot-aided methods due to its simplicity and reliability. By taking advantage of the channel sparseness, compressive sensing (CS) can be utilized for channel estimation with much fewer pilot symbols. In this paper, orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) is employed to reconstruct channel impulse response. We evaluate the performance in terms of NMSE and BER. The simulation results shown that OMP algorithm outperforms LS in channel estimation with more efficient number of pilots. The BER performance also gives only slight difference compared to the system with known channel coefficient.

articleTitle: Design of Array Antenna Using Proximity Coupled Feeding and Multi-Layer Parasitic for C-Band Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna array design for weather radar applications using proximity coupled feeding and multi-layer parasitic techniques is described. The purpose of this antenna array design is to increase the gain and bandwidth performance of the microstrip antenna with an efficient number of elements. In this study, the proposed antenna design uses FR-4 epoxy material with = 4.3 at C-Band frequency. The proposed antenna design achieves a bandwidth of up to 1.243 GHz and a gain of 12.2 dBi. These results prove that the use of proximity coupled feeding technique and additional of the multi-layer parasitic can improve the performance of the antenna array. Thus, the antenna array design using this technique can be used as the basis for developing portable weather radar antennas and other radar applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of SIW Phase Shifter Types with Mode Matching Technique (MMT)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper uses Mode Matching Technique (MMT) to study and analyze three types of Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) phase shifters. Three design equations are presented and used to design three-phase shifter prototypes. The designed phase shifters are analyzed with MMT and full-wave simulator CST and the results are compared and discussed. The cascading procedure in SIW structure is achieved by the help of Generalized Scattering Matrix Method (GSMM).

articleTitle: Design Consideration of Data Acquisition System for Capacitive Plantar Pressure Insole
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Gait, the term used to describe the manner in which people move while they walk, varies according to walking style, aging, illnesses, and accidents. It can be used to predict the diabetes course and disorders associated with the motor nervous system. A capacitive pressure sensor (CPS) can be employed as the plantar sensor when the user is walking. In order to improve the linearity of CPS, a data acquisition system (DAQ) based on the LC resonant principle that can decrease unanticipated EMI has been developed. The result demonstrates that the change in capacitance is linearly proportional to the pressure change. However, parasitic capacitance, thermal noise, body capacitance, and other factors still affect error and offset. Finally, further work is needed to improve the capacitance sensitivity of the plantar sensor.

articleTitle: Wearable Fabric Based-Biosensor for Ion Detection in Sweat
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Sweat is a biomarker that contains ions and biochemical compounds that may reflect human health conditions. Wearable biosensors enable the collection and analysis of sweat in situ, noninvasive, real-time, continuous monitoring of biochemical compounds. This paper presents the development and characterization of wearable biosensors for ion detection in sweat. The screen-printed method was used for the fabrication of a working electrode and a reference electrode on cotton fabric. The reference electrode was constructed from Ag/AgCl ink. The working electrode is constructed from a modified carbon electrode, conducting polymer, and an ion-selective membrane. Artificial sweat with known compositions was used for biosensor validation. The biosensors had been used to detect the sodium and potassium ions in sweat from patients with soft activities.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Implementation of I/Q Chirp Signal Generator Using Memory-Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In this study, we evaluated the I/Q chirp signal generator using a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) to be implemented for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) application. A chirp signal is a sinusoidal signal with a constant amplitude that, over a brief period of time, either increases in frequency from low to high (up-chirp) or decreases in frequency from high to low (down-chirp). To simplify our proposed design, a memory-based technique is employed to store the generated output chirp signal where the in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) signals are stored in a rom-based look-up table separately. To reduce circuit usage, a single accumulator that points to the address of both look-up tables is leveraged to generate the I/Q chirp signal through dual-channel DAC chips. From the experimental results, by using an Altera Cyclone IV FPGA, we demonstrated the capability of the system to generate the I/Q chirp signal at 10 MHz of bandwidth for a period of 10 μs.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of All-Dielectric Metasurface Structure for LiDAR Beamsteering in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Optical beam steering is important for applications such as Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR). Currently, most commercial LiDARs rely on mechanical rotation to direct the optical beam, resulting in a mechanical LiDAR scan rate that is not optimal for applications such as autonomous vehicles. The metasurface-based beam steering system is believed to have the potential to fulfill all the challenges above. However, low efficiency and wide field of view are still a challenge. Therefore, a disc-shaped all-dielectric metasurface structure for the beam steering system is proposed. The proposed structure was optimized and investigated using electromagnetic analysis simulation software. By varying the geometrical dimensions of the meta-atoms, the optimal size is obtained at the wavelength of the C-Band Optical regime. In addition, the transmission of the output beam deflected by an angle of 45° was achieved. Based on these results, the proposed structure can be a reference for developing beam steering system designs for autonomous vehicle applications in the future.

articleTitle: Toward A Compact and Reconfigurable Radar-UAV for Remote Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The use of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) borne radar for search and rescue missions in post-disaster areas interests many researchers in recent years. In the case of the large observation area, effective and efficient technology is mandatory for the success of the mission to reduce the affected death toll. Since time is a challenging constraint in this mission, the use of multiple, compact, and small radar-UAV is the most prospective solution. Besides, the flexible and reconfigurable system is also desirable for easing the operation. Thus, this paper presents the development of a compact and reconfigurable radar-UAV employing software-defined radio-based radar and a small quadcopter. The development progress and preliminary result of evaluation and test of the developed prototype are presented and discussed thoroughly.

articleTitle: A Novel Parasitic EBG Structure to Enhance Mutual Coupling for 2.45 GHz MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In the 5.0 industrial era, antenna technology has been evolving very rapidly. Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) is expected as a method to increase channel capacity and reliability. The structure of the MIMO antenna should be observed to avoid the mutual coupling between elements. A novel circular square parasitic electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure is evaluated for MIMO in 2.45 GHz frequency to improve the mutual coupling effect. A simple two identical circular patches design with the multiple parasitic EBG structure is optimized using HFSS. The overall dimensions of the microstrip antenna because of the design optimization are 50.3 mm x 115.7 mm. The results demonstrate that the antenna has slightly -16 dB of S11 by simulation and measurement, whereas the mutual coupling effect was decreased at slightly -23.5 dB and -25.08 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Stacked Patch Antenna with Cross-Slot Circular Polarization for GPS Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A design of a dual-band circularly polarized GPS (L1 and L2) receiver has been proposed. This antenna design utilizes the concept of a stacked antenna that feeds through a single coaxial cable. Two radiators are placed on top of the stacked substrate to obtain the dual-band frequency. The probe feed and the chamfered corners on the radiators generate circular polarization. A cross slot applies to the top layer patch to miniaturize antenna dimension and improve the axial ratio. The L1 and L2 bandwidths of the proposed antenna are 71 MHz and 74 MHz, respectively. Both resonant bands' axial ratio bandwidth (3dB) is 18 MHz.

articleTitle: On the Importance of the Accuracy of the Estimate of the Radar Position for Fully Coherent Jamming of a Stripmap SAR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has become a standard sensor for military intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance-based operations. Jamming of SAR sensors has become an important topic, especially to deny the use of the sensor or to induce false targets into the image to degrade the response time of a military user. A SAR sensor uses coherent integration of radar pulses to generate cross-range resolution during the creation of an image of an area. A jammer thus has to recreate an accurate representation of the phase trajectory of the radar pulse train to induce false targets into the SAR image. To achieve this, the jammer requires an accurate estimate of the position of the SAR sensor. This paper presents a simulation-based analysis of the accuracy with which a jammer is required to estimate the position of the SAR platform to enable fully coherent jamming. Fully coherent jamming is required for effective deception jamming of SAR sensors. The results show that angular accuracies in the order of millidegrees and range accuracies in the order of 10’s of metres are required to achieve fully coherent jamming against an X-band SAR.

articleTitle: Design and Realization Bandpass Filter 2.4 GHz Rectangular Microstrip Using Stepped Impedance Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper purposed to show the design, simulation and realization of a bandpass filter using stepped impedance resonators for a 2.4 GHz communication system. The rectangular shape was used to design the proposed bandpass filter. Furthermore, the stepped impedance resonators with some modification and adjustment have been used to get a good response of insertion loss, return loss and bandwidth. The roger 5880, with a thickness of 0.787 mm and a dielectric constant of 2.2, was used for simulation and realization. As a result, the measured optimum response for return loss is -30.43 dB, insertion loss is -1.75 dB, and the bandwidth is 120 MHz.

articleTitle: Application of Down-conversion Materials based on Trivalent Europium Ion-doped Fluoroborotellurite Glass for Transparent Dye-sensitized Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The development of down-conversion materials on fluoroborotellurite glass and its application in transparent dye-sensitized solar cells have been reported in the present work. The down-conversion layer Eu³⁺: glass was prepared from 0.0, 0.1, 1.0, and 1.5 of Eu₂O₃ with B₂O₃, TeO₂, ZnF₂, and BaO using conventional melt and quenching technique. Meanwhile, the fabrication of transparent DSSC was performed using a screen printing technique. The absorption and the emission spectra of the Eu³⁺:glass were characterized, while the electrical performance of the DSSC coupled with Eu³⁺:glass was measured via current-voltage (I-V) characterization. The emission of Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:glass was found at 588, 613, 649, and 702 nm under an excitation wavelength of 392 nm, while the absorption of dye solution was recorded from 330 to 800 nm. The results show that further investigation of Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:glass coupled with other types of dye solutions is required to find the most suitable DSSC for Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:glass as a DC layer.

articleTitle: Dual-Input Cascaded DC-DC Converter for Hydromechanical Energy Harvesting in a Hydroponic System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: In a hydroponic system, water is used as a growing medium. Water will circulate nutrients throughout the plant on the grow tray. To maintain the nutritional balance of the whole plant, water circulation should be done continuously for 24 hours. This water will flow back to the reservoir by using the force of gravity. Therefore, at a certain height, this force will produce potential energy and influence the water flow rate. Despite its small size, this energy can be harvested and used to power a low-power load, such as a wireless sensor node (WSN) in a hydroponic monitoring system. To harvest this energy, a small electrical energy conversion from more than one micro-water turbine requires a well-designed converter. Therefore, in this research, a dual-input cascade DC-DC boost converter is designed to process the power from the turbine. The topology of the converter uses a basic-boost converter circuit, but it is combined with a parallel-series connection. The experiment results show that the converter works as expected.

articleTitle: Reverse Vending Machine Using TCRT5000 and Inductive Proximity Sensors for Bottles and Cans Sorting
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Garbage has always been a problem in Indonesia. One root is the lack interest in throwing them in their proper place. Additionally, the waste that has been disposed is not managed properly. In response to it, the authors designed a trash bin as a Reverse Vending Machine (RVM) with the ability to detect bottles and cans and provide rewards for the person. The machine was able to detect bottles by using the TCRT5000 sensor and cans by using an inductive proximity sensor. Both trashes were also sorted to a specific trash bin directly, and the reward was calculated directly based on the total of bottles and cans put into it. A push button can be pressed to print out the ticket, but it would decline the request when there is no bottles or cans input. In addition, ultrasonic sensors were installed to automatically check the trash bins of the RVM, and LEDs were used to notify the user whether the trash bin of the bottles or cans were already full or not. After 24 attempts of testing, the successful rate was found to be 100%.

articleTitle: A Notch Filter Design and Realization using Cross-coupled Line Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper presents a notch filter with coupled line structure. The filter works at a center frequency of 3 GHz for S-Band applications. A good rejection filter, narrow bandwidth, and compact filter are needed to improve the performance of a notch filter. The proposed notch filter comprises four coupled lines arranged like a cross-coupled. Based on the even-mode and odd-mode characteristic impedance of the parallel-coupled line filter, the dimensions of coupled lines were calculated. An electromagnetic software simulation was used to investigate and optimize the design. In this structure, the other coupling in the center of the structure occurred. Two kinds of bends in the center of the structure were applied to acquire the performance based on the specification. From the simulation results, all the bends showed a good performance. The fabrication and measurement of the notch filter on RT/duroid 5880 as a substrate were done to validate the proposed design. The fabricated notch filter has a size of 50 mm x 50 mm. As a result, the input reflection coefficient (S11) and insertion loss (S21) at working frequency have good agreement with the specification. The difference is in the bandwidth, where the bandwidth is reduced by 15 % from the required specification, which may be caused by the fabrication process.

articleTitle: Webots-Based: Design of Collision Free Trajectory of Wheeled Mobile Robot Using Artificial Potential Field
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Wheeled mobile robot (WMR) is widely used in everyday life. The problem that arises in its implementation is navigation. Besides that, integrating navigation components, especially path planning, in a WMR kinematic model is considered very important to produce natural robot motion. One of the reliable path planning algorithms that can be used in real-time is Artificial Potential Field (APF). The weakness of this algorithm is that it can be stuck at the local minimum. Modification of APF (MAPF) which several researchers have proposed, serves to solve the drawbacks of this algorithm. This study aims to integrate and implement navigation capabilities in the WMR kinematics model, especially path planning. The test was carried out in a simulation using the Webots simulator. The robot used is an E-puck robot. E-puck is a differential drive mobile robot (DDMR) that uses two drivers to move. The results show that the MAPF path planning algorithm can be implemented well in the WMR kinematics model. Local minimum problems in the form of symmetrically aligned robot-obstacle-goal (SAROG) and goal non-reachable due to obstacle nearby (GNRON) in real conditions can be solved properly.

articleTitle: Image Processing: Manual Segmentation on 3D Femur Bone Model
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Image processing popularly reconstructs the original image to become the intended image that reveals certain information. In the medical field, a technique of image processing, particularly segmentation, is a fundamental step for further analysis. This study aims to segment the femur bone in a three-dimensional (3D) model from the whole image area of the lower extremity for any other medical purpose, such as implant or surgery planning. This study's segmentation is building a specific algorithm using Matlab. This technique is considered to eliminate the drawbacks of automated software in the segmentation process, such as DICOM viewer and analyzing software with inconsistent accuracy and purchase at high cost. Results from this study show that the segmented femur model has more prolonged, about 30%, than the original image. Although the measurement also finds significant differences between automatic and manual segmentation, this trial significantly increases knowledge of the possibility of using manual segmentation to solve problems while using the DICOM viewer software.

articleTitle: Organometallic Dyes Modification on the NiOx Hole Transport Layer for Organic Photovoltaic Application
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Nickel oxide (NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) has proved as an efficient hole transport layer (HTL) for perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with inverted structure. However, NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is rarely adopted as HTL for standard structure organic photovoltaics (OPVs) with PEDOT:PSS still widely used despite their drawbacks that could affect the device's operational stability. Passivation of NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/perovskite interface with self-assembled monolayer or organometallic dye could increase the performance of single junction inverted PSCs by suppressing defect densities at the interface of NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>. However, their application in OPVs has not been explored. This work investigates the effect of NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> passivation with various organometallic dye molecules (N719, C106, N3, N749, Z907) for OPV application. Our results show that only NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>-based devices modified with N3 exhibit an efficiency increase compared to those with pristine NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> HTL. This work provides insights into the role of the energy alignment between the NiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> interface with the OPV's active layer.

articleTitle: Microstrip Transmitarray Antenna with Three Layered 5x5 Crosslet and Square Slot Patches at 38 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This research aims to design a transmitarray antenna. The three layers of Crosslet and square slot in 5×5 array is designed and tested for 38 GHz frequency. In the design, we exploit the phase characteristics of the transmission coefficient through the whole structure. A phase shift of up to 233° can be achieved by variation of the length of the Crosslet and the square slot. The antenna size of 20 mm x 20 mm was fabricated using Roger RT4003C and measured. According to the simulation results, a gain of 23.29 dBi is obtained oriented to the horizontal direction as expected from the design view of the point.

articleTitle: Investigation on Frequency and Radius Dependence in Vertical and Horizontal Antenna Alignments of UCA-based OAM Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to further investigate the communication with Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) waves between two OAM antenna arrays. The antenna arrays consist of individual dipoles, which together form a Uniform Circular Array (UCA). In this paper, two configurations that have already been discovered are assumed, in which there is no crosstalk between the individual modes. On the one hand, the vertical alignment already examined by many papers and on the other hand a horizontal alignment in which the dipoles have a certain rotation around the axis. The first investigation deals with the frequency dependency in OAM communication in the given setup. In a further investigation, the influence of the radius of the antenna arrays is conducted. The simulations will focus on the transmission of the individual OAM modes and the crosstalk between different OAM modes.

articleTitle: The Development of Human Machine Interface (HMI) Based Graphical User Interface (GUI) for Telecontrol System of a Ship Mounted Two-DoF Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The development of a telecontrol system for a ship-mounted two-DoF manipulator is greatly required since it must be controlled from the control room of a ship and subjected to random ocean waves. This paper addresses such a task by developing a human-machine interface (HMI) based graphical user interface (GUI). The features cover control and monitoring of the manipulator system as well as object tracking. The HMI is embedded in a console box via a personal computer (PC) and capable of accessing sensors and actuators through a microcontroller. Data processing and communication techniques are also proposed to avoid overlap or lag for real-time implementation. Experimental results show that the telecontrol system successfully monitors and control the manipulator system as well as track the objects using an image processing algorithm.

articleTitle: Utilizing Smartphone as Colorimetric Sensor in Detecting Stress Level
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Stress is a human reaction that occurs when there is a physical or emotional change in the environment that necessitates adaptation. The human body produces stress hormones known as cortisol. When we are under stress, the amount of cortisol in our bodies increases. Cortisol levels can also reveal health information. In this paper, we developed an Android application on a smartphone as a colorimetric sensor to measure cortisol concentration, which was correlated with stress level as part of the development of a wearable cortisol biosensor. The smartphone’s Android apps can detect changes in the color of the biosensor caused by cortisol concentration changes. This color will be translated by a smartphone into Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) values, which will then be translated into the stress level.

articleTitle: Design and Prototyping of High Gain Horn Antennas for Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Continuous wave radar with frequency modulation offers a promising solution for imaging applications in low visibility, obscure conditions. In this type of radar, two antennas are used; one for transmission and another for reception. In this paper, we present the optimal design of high-gain low-cost antennas for such imaging radars to operate in Sri Lanka’s unlicensed band within 2.4 – 2.5 GHz which also is an unlicensed band globally. The radar performance can be improved with a properly optimized pair of antennas at the transmitter and receiver. This paper presents the antenna design procedure we adopted along with simulations using CST Studio Suite 2021. Although we studied pyramidal horn and cylindrical horn antennas, we concluded that pyramidal horns are prohibitively large in size compared to cylindrical horns for comparable performance. The constructed cylindrical horn antennas were tested using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) and the test results well matched with the simulations. The antennas were also tested by including them in the radar prototype. The results of tracking performance with varying polarization modes indicate that the use of same polarization at the transmit and receive antennas give the best performance.

articleTitle: Solution Processed Non-Fullerene All Small Molecules Solar Cell Using Perylene Diimide Acceptor Material
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: A perylene diimide (PDI) is successfully applied as acceptor material in organic small molecules solar cell combining with two-dimensional (2D) conjugated small molecules benzodithiophene (BDT) donor material that 2,6-Bis[2,5-bis(3-octylrhodanine)-(3,3-dioctyl-2,2':5,2''-terthiophene)]-4,8-bis((5-ethylhexyl) thiophen-2-yl) benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b'] dithiophene or SMPV1 for all small molecules solar cell device. This non-fullerene solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 2.51%. It is presumably related to the PDI crystal formation during thermal annealing and effect of the additive. These result promise PDI small molecule as potential acceptor for all small molecule organic solar cells.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of RIS-aided Multicell 5G and Beyond Wireless Cellular Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Huge demands of multimedia traffic through wireless cellular communication networks force researchers to find innovative ways to improve the capacity and service qualities of the networks. Reconfigurable Intelligence Surfaces (RISs) have received much attentions and have emerged as a potential candidate for the next generation of wireless cellular communication networks, i.e., the 5G and beyond, since RIS offers many advantages. On the other hand, the multicell wireless cellular communication network faces signal blockages, especially in urban areas. In addition to this issue, the multicell scenario of wireless cellular communication networks faces interference problems due to its frequency reuse property. The interference situation becomes worse when we apply the frequency reuse factor (FRF) of 1. This paper proposes the use of RIS to study its effects in reducing the blockage and interference issues in multicell wireless cellular communication networks. Single RIS are deployed in three cells of a wireless cellular network scenario. Extensive simulation experiments have been carried out. The performance parameters in terms of Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR), throughput, and Bit Error Rate (BER) have been measured, collected, and analyzed. The simulation results show that the system with RIS, compared to the system without RIS with obstacle loss of 60 dB, achieved the performance improvements: 10.48 dB of SINR increase, 207.7% of throughput increase, and 22.74% of BER decrease.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost TDS Sensor Using an Electric Plug with The Curve Fitting Method Approaches
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: This paper introduces the development of a low-cost total dissolved solids (TDS) sensor system using an electric plug type C (Indonesian standard electric plug) as the probe. The TDS value is normally identified based on the drop voltage between the plug’s pins, representing the water resistance value. In our developed system design, the TDS data were collected and processed by a low-cost microcontroller using a 10-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Several samples of TDS solutions were made, ranging from approximately 300 to 1500 ppm for the experiment. Then, the ADC values from those solutions, which represent the drop voltage and the water resistance values, were measured and collected. Once the data were collected, three curve fitting techniques (exponential, polynomial, and power) were used to construct graph equation formulas. Finally, the acquired equations were compared using a reversed comparison technique to determine the best equation to apply. The experimental results showed that an electric plug type C as an electrical conductivity (EC) probe had a high capacity to be used as a TDS sensor in our system. The polynomial model matched the TDS graph with a lower root mean squared error (RMSE) value. Moreover, the accurate measurement was followed by an error tolerance of less than 8.2%. From this result, we are fully confident that our TDS sensor system is still suitable for hydroponic and aquaponic monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Time Series Land Subsidence Analysis Based on Persistent Scattered Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar Method of Jakarta City Region Using Terra SAR X Spaceborne Data
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Scientists have widely used remote sensing technology to observe surface phenomena, either happened by naturally or artificially. Land subsidence monitoring is one of the promising discoveries made by implementing remote sensing technology, particularly with radar images. The gap in radar image processing technology has been attempted to solve in this study with a real case study in Jakarta, Indonesia. The challenge of simplifying the complex processing step that involved different correction due to time acquisition in radar images have been explained in this study. Aside from that, many researchers believe excessive groundwater extraction and over-exploitation of groundwater can be caused land subsidence, though other factors like land deformation and geological change can accelerate the possibilities. Prior studies have illustrated the subsidence level and methodology to investigate how subsurface change can be indicated by radar image scattering. According to that, this study focused on subsidence escalation in Jakarta. Although other areas can have similar issues, further study will be required. In this study, the Persistent Scatterer Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PS-InSAR) method has been used in Terra SAR-X multitemporal data; the process strives to search for the indication of land subsidence in the study area. The benefit of this PS-InSAR is its capability to extract point clouds at a particular temporal coherence setting from the SAR image, representing a current surface level. The data has been collected and processed from 29 scenes from 2017 to 2021, thus showing the changes over the last four years. Analysis during that period found that land subsidence existed at a high rate, compared with 2017 data, perceived that in 2021 subsidence level was cumulatively around 9.85 cm in the Pantai Indah Kapuk, North Jakarta area, and 5.63 cm in the Kembangan area of West Jakarta. A ground check is needed to ensure this strongly connects with geological factors. Still, PS-InSAR can be a beneficial tool for the surface modelling in a broad area and rapid mapping for geoscience analysis.

articleTitle: Sampling Time Value Determination Method for Designing a Real-time Control System with Non-deterministic Time Elements such as Rotary Encoder and SPI
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Different articles have published serial communication characteristics measurements for real-time control system (RCS). However, most of them focused on latency time measurements. Articles addressing a specific case with a combination of non-deterministic time elements such as rotary encoder (RE) and serial peripheral interface (SPI) are limited. This paper proposed a method to cope with a non-deterministic time due to the RE pulse timing by using a separate processor to handle pulse signals from the RE and time delay measurements of the SPI signal. It investigated the consumption time of each process, i.e., reading sensor signal, calculating control command, and sending control command. We used a microcontroller instead of a personal or industrial computer since the control system will be embedded in an electric vehicle (EV) for drive-by-wire (DbW) function. We obtained the experimental results of 4.42 µs and 6 µs for reading the sensor signal and sending the control command, respectively. The microcontroller required 1.2 µs to complete a simple control command calculation. The approach presented in this paper can generally be used for sampling time value determination in designing a RCS using the RE as sensor and SPI for sending the control command signals to the actuators. We obtained the appropriate sampling time value of 25 ms. It will be used for designing a feedback controller.

articleTitle: Investigation of Microwave Absorption Properties on Oil Palm Shell-derived Activated Carbon
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: The demand of microwave and radar-absorbing materials has increased in military and electronics applications. Microwave absorber, as well as radar absorber material, has been studied recently to overcome the EMI problem. An absorber material with lightweight, thin, eco-friendly, broadband, and high absorption efficiency are highly desirable to fabricate the radar absorber. Biomass-based activated carbon is known to have excellent absorption performance. In this manuscript, we investigate the microwave absorption properties in the X-band region from 8 GHz to 12 GHz of oil palm shell (OPS)-derived activated carbon. We found the enhancement S11 parameter up to -32.61 dB after the OPS transformed into activated carbon OPS through KOH activation and physical carbonization. The porous structure of activated carbon OPS corresponds to the better microwave absorption properties that correlate with better attenuation and impedance matching. This result shows that OPS-derived activated carbon is a promising lightweight, nature-based material for radar absorber applications.

articleTitle: Microfluidic for supporting Fiber-optic-based Surface Plasmon Resonance sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Radar, Antenna, Microwave, Electronics, and Telecommunications (ICRAMET)
abstract: Microfluidic has been developed to be applied as sensor and sensor support because of its small size (in the micrometer range), compact structure, low analyte consumption and can be integrated into a chip. The combination of microfluidic and optical systems (optical fiber) has been widely used among microfluidic-based sensors. Based on its sensing principle, an optical fiber-based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is very promising for detecting bacteria, viruses, chemical molecules, etc. In this paper, we discuss microfluidics research for supporting fiber-optic sensors in detail, such as device fabrication and application of integrated microfluidic-optical fiber-based SPR sensors. Factors affecting sensitivity, such as the gold layer thickness, and the effect of the sensing area were studied through simulation to strengthen the understanding of the sensor.
